> **Rebase update — October 11, 2026:** Head `eecbd16e` is rebased onto main snapshot `fcae5c98`. Focused validation: **101 passed**, with all applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passing. [Exact commands, logs, source mapping and limitations](https://github.com/NolenLiang/vllm/blob/c4f6bfdd11c2718f767b85c82ed2af8314dd8135/pr-rebase-evidence/20261011/README.md). The maintainer's Mamba2 RFC/hold discussion remains in effect; this update does not request re-review.
>
> The GPU/model results and first-person human review statements below retain their original pre-rebase revision attribution. Codex performed this rebase and the new checks; fresh human review/personal test execution and model-level/multi-GPU validation are not attested here. Draft status is unchanged.

## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the Mamba2 SSD kernels (`_bmm_chunk_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, `_state_passing_fwd_kernel`) still pick their tile configuration by autotuning. The autotune keys exclude batch and sequence length, so one process is consistent with itself, but the choice is made by timing and can differ between processes, for example a trainer rescoring a rollout and the inference engine, or two engine restarts. The tile changes the reduction order and therefore the bits: on GB200 with chunk size 64 and 8 heads, `BLOCK_SIZE_H` 2 versus 8 or 64 in the chunk cumsum gives different fp32 prefix sums and 59 to 351 of about one million output elements differ.

This PR pins each of the five kernels to one of its existing candidates under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. The pin is applied to the autotuner right after each kernel definition, so the candidate lists are not touched and default mode autotunes exactly as before. #55627 and #55905 build on this: they compare decode bits against prefill bits from these kernels, so the tile has to be fixed rather than timed.

Not a duplicate: #54993 and #55627 change how Mamba2 prefill and decode run, not the kernels' autotune selection. #48213 adds CPU-tuned candidate lists for the Triton CPU backend; since this PR leaves the lists alone, the two do not overlap.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py
```

The new file checks the pin helper, that each pinned tile is one of the kernel's candidates and that under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` each kernel exposes exactly that one configuration, and that the rows of a prefix do not depend on the tokens that follow.

## Test Result

GB200, Triton 3.7.1. Default mode: 7 passed. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: 101 passed, the new tests plus the existing SSD correctness suite on the pinned tiles. Default-mode outputs are unchanged by construction (same candidate lists, keys and kernels), so no model evaluation is attached; the batch-invariant mode is exercised end to end by #55627 and #55905. pre-commit passes on the changed files.

## AI assistance

AI tools assisted with the implementation, tests and documentation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

For the training side of the alignment claim: Megatron's deterministic mode (`MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC=1`, without `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=1`) already pins its vendored SSD kernels to one configuration per kernel, the cheapest candidate by block product times stages. On Triton 3.7.1 that is M64/N32/K32 (5 stages, 2 warps) for bmm, chunk_state and chunk_scan, `BLOCK_SIZE_H=2` for the cumsum and `BLOCK_SIZE=64` for state passing. Those differ from the tiles pinned here only in N, stages and warps, and the SSD + gate + norm kernel composition of vLLM batch-invariant mode versus Megatron's `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen(z=...)` is bitwise identical for the granite-350m and Nemotron-H shapes at chunk 128 and 256 (16/16 comparisons, out-of-tree script). Pinning vLLM to Megatron's exact picks gives the same result, so the bits depend on `BLOCK_SIZE_K` (and on the M tile of the row-gated emit kernel in #55905), not on N, stages or warps. With autotuning on both sides the chunk-128 cases differ, which is the reason for pinning at all.

A correction to my earlier note here. Megatron's training path calls the SSD kernels of the `mamba_ssm` package (`mamba_split_conv1d_scan_combined`), not the copy vendored under `megatron/core/ssm/ops`, which serves the varlen inference paths; my "only N, stages and warps differ" statement was about that vendored copy. `mamba_ssm` has the same `MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC` cheapest-config rule and, on the commit NeMo RL pins, selects the same M64/N32/K32 tiles but `BLOCK_SIZE_H=1` for the chunk cumsum (its candidate list includes 1; the list here starts at 2). Stage by stage, with the same cumsum fed in, every other kernel is bitwise identical across the two stacks; the cumsum itself depends on the head tile, and the two cumsum kernels agree with each other at H=2 for chunk sizes 128 and 256 while diverging at H=1 for chunk 256 (GB200, Triton 3.7.1, Granite-350M and Nemotron-H-8B shapes). So the tile pinned here stays at H=2 and the training side needs the same value; that currently requires a change in `mamba_ssm`, which I will propose there. With #55627 + #55895 + #55905 + #56244 + #52905 and H=2 on both sides, under one fixed setup (GB200, bf16, TP=1, eager prefill of a single 578-token prompt), the first Mamba layer of Nemotron-H-8B-Base is bitwise identical between the Megatron training forward and vLLM batch-invariant mode; the next MLP layer's RMSNorm is the first observed divergence, and subsequent layers then receive different inputs.

@tdoublep @yewentao256 would one of you have a look when you get a chance? This is the first and smallest piece of the batch-invariant Mamba2 stack tracked in #55524: it pins the SSD Triton autotune configs under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` so prefill, chunked prefill and decode run the same tiles (the default candidate lists are unchanged). #55627, #55905 and #56244 are stacked on it and are now out of draft.
@tomeras91 looping you in here as well: this is the base of the batch-invariant Mamba2 stack (#55627, #55905, #56244) and only pins the SSD Triton autotune configs under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.

Pushed the smaller version (fd6d1e8fd). The candidate lists are untouched now; each kernel gets one `pin_autotune_config(kernel, config)` call after its definition, which swaps the autotuner's configs for the pinned one under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. 6 files, +195/-3 including the test. Tests on GB200 are in the description, the existing SSD suite passes on the pinned tiles.
Rebased on current main, no change to the content.

Okay, I will put the current PRs on hold. This PR has already been integrated into the downstream PRs https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/55 and https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/vllm/pull/25 to support batch invariance for Nemotron 3.5; please take a look at the implementation to see if it aligns with your expectations or if you think it might be useful.

@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT the Mamba2 SSD (chunked scan) kernels run one fixed
+Triton configuration instead of autotuning, and the rows of a prefix must not
+depend on the tokens that follow it."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops import (
+    ssd_bmm,
+    ssd_chunk_scan,
+    ssd_chunk_state,
+    ssd_state_passing,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.ssd_combined import (
+    mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.triton_helpers import pin_autotune_config
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+CHUNK = 64
+NHEADS, HEAD_DIM, NGROUPS, DSTATE = 8, 64, 1, 64
+
+
+@triton.autotune(
+    configs=[triton.Config({"BLOCK": 64}), triton.Config({"BLOCK": 128})],
+    key=[],
+)
+@triton.jit
+def _dummy_kernel(x_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    pass
+
+
+def test_pin_autotune_config_follows_the_environment(monkeypatch):
+    pinned = triton.Config({"BLOCK": 256})
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", False)
+    pin_autotune_config(_dummy_kernel, pinned)
+    assert len(_dummy_kernel.configs) == 2
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", True)
+    pin_autotune_config(_dummy_kernel, pinned)
+    assert _dummy_kernel.configs == [pinned]
+
+
+# (autotuned kernel, its pinned configuration)
+SSD_KERNELS = [
+    (ssd_bmm._bmm_chunk_fwd_kernel, ssd_bmm._BATCH_INVARIANT_CONFIG),
+    (
+        ssd_chunk_state._chunk_cumsum_fwd_kernel,
+        ssd_chunk_state._CUMSUM_BATCH_INVARIANT_CONFIG,
+    ),
+    (
+        ssd_chunk_state._chunk_state_fwd_kernel,
+        ssd_chunk_state._CHUNK_STATE_BATCH_INVARIANT_CONFIG,
+    ),
+    (ssd_chunk_scan._chunk_scan_fwd_kernel, ssd_chunk_scan._BATCH_INVARIANT_CONFIG),
+    (
+        ssd_state_passing._state_passing_fwd_kernel,
+        ssd_state_passing._BATCH_INVARIANT_CONFIG,
+    ),
+]
+
+
+def _key(config):
+    return (tuple(sorted(config.kwargs.items())), config.num_warps, config.num_stages)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kernel,pinned", SSD_KERNELS)
+def test_ssd_kernel_configs(kernel, pinned):
+    """Pinned at import under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT; otherwise the pinned tile is
+    one of the untouched default candidates."""
+    keys = [_key(c) for c in kernel.configs]
+    if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:
+        assert keys == [_key(pinned)]
+    else:
+        assert len(keys) > 1 and keys.count(_key(pinned)) == 1
+
+
+def _scan(x, dt, B, C, A, dt_bias, D):
+    length = x.shape[0]
+    n_chunks = -(-length // CHUNK)
+    i32 = lambda v: torch.tensor(v, dtype=torch.int32, device=x.device)  # noqa: E731
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen(
+        x,
+        dt,
+        A,
+        B,
+        C,
+        chunk_size=CHUNK,
+        cu_seqlens=i32([0, length]),
+        cu_chunk_seqlens=i32([k * CHUNK for k in range(n_chunks)] + [length]),
+        last_chunk_indices=i32([n_chunks - 1]),
+        seq_idx=i32([0] * n_chunks),
+        out=out,
+        D=D,
+        z=None,
+        dt_bias=dt_bias,
+        initial_states=None,
+        dt_softplus=True,
+        dt_limit=(0.0, float("inf")),
+        state_dtype=torch.float32,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(),
+    reason="Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels require a CUDA-alike device.",
+)
+def test_ssd_is_prefix_invariant():
+    """The rows of a prefix do not depend on the tokens that follow it."""
+    device = torch.device(current_platform.device_type)
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+    A = -(torch.rand(NHEADS, device=device, generator=gen) * 15 + 1)
+    dt_bias = torch.log(
+        torch.expm1(torch.rand(NHEADS, device=device, generator=gen) * 0.09 + 0.01)
+    )
+    D = torch.ones(NHEADS, device=device)
+    bf = torch.bfloat16
+    x = torch.randn(400, NHEADS, HEAD_DIM, device=device, generator=gen).to(bf)
+    dt = (0.5 * torch.randn(400, NHEADS, device=device, generator=gen)).to(bf)
+    B = torch.randn(400, NGROUPS, DSTATE, device=device, generator=gen).to(bf)
+    C = torch.randn(400, NGROUPS, DSTATE, device=device, generator=gen).to(bf)
+    full = _scan(x, dt, B, C, A, dt_bias, D)
+    for n in (37, CHUNK, 150, 2 * CHUNK + 5):
+        prefix = _scan(x[:n], dt[:n], B[:n], C[:n], A, dt_bias, D)
+        assert torch.equal(prefix.view(torch.int16), full[:n].view(torch.int16)), n

 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
+import vllm.envs as envs
 from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
 
 
@@ -15,3 +16,16 @@ def fast_exp(x):
     # exp(x) = exp2(x * log2(e)), where log2(e) = 1/ln(2) = 1.4426950408889634
     LOG2E = tl.constexpr(1.4426950408889634)
     return tl.math.exp2(LOG2E * x)
+
+
+def pin_autotune_config(kernel, config: triton.Config) -> None:
+    """Under ``VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`` make an autotuned kernel always run ``config``.
+
+    Autotuning picks a tile by timing, so two processes that share these kernels
+    (a trainer and an inference engine, or two engine restarts) can settle on
+    different tiles, and the tile changes the reduction order and therefore the
+    bits. The default candidate lists are left as they are.
+    """
+    if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:
+        kernel.configs = [config]
+        kernel.cache.clear()

Megatron's training path calls the SSD kernels of the `mamba_ssm` package (`mamba_split_conv1d_scan_combined`), not the copy vendored under `megatron/core/ssm/ops`, which serves the varlen inference paths; my "only N, stages and warps differ" statement was about that vendored copy. `mamba_ssm` has the same `MAMBA_DETERMINISTIC` cheapest-config rule and, on the commit NeMo RL pins, selects the same M64/N32/K32 tiles but `BLOCK_SIZE_H=1` for the chunk cumsum (its candidate list includes 1; the list here starts at 2). Stage by stage, with the same cumsum fed in, every other kernel is bitwise identical across the two stacks; the cumsum itself depends on the head tile, and the two cumsum kernels agree with each other at H=2 for chunk sizes 128 and 256 while diverging at H=1 for chunk 256 (GB200, Triton 3.7.1, Granite-350M and Nemotron-H-8B shapes). So the tile pinned here stays at H=2 and the training side needs the same value; that currently requires a change in `mamba_ssm`, which I will propose there. With #55627 + #55895 + #55905 + #56244 + #52905 and H=2 on both sides, under one fixed setup (GB200, bf16, TP=1, eager prefill of a single 578-token prompt), the first Mamba layer of Nemotron-H-8B-Base is bitwise identical between the Megatron training forward and vLLM batch-invariant mode; the next MLP layer's RMSNorm is the first observed divergence, and subsequent layers then receive different inputs.

@tdoublep @yewentao256 would one of you have a look when you get a chance?
